claim: Apple platform identifiers are H+generation+tier-letter (H16G = M4 base, H17C = M5 Max); the generation number is shared between A and M chips of the same year and tier letters for M-series are G=base, S=Pro, C=Max, D=Ultra, M=reduced-core Max, so no component of an h1N-style arch string encodes a core count.
source: user-provided Apple Wiki + Asahi Linux cross-reference 2026-10-11; ours: T8132+h16g mini (API-138), AppleT6050PMGR on Mac17,14, h17c compiler target; paper glossary T8142->H-generation (results/EXP-024-engine-attribution/raw/research-2026-10-06/ane_paper_sec20_sec33_extracts.md ~L20571)
caveat: applewiki.com 403s from this network so the user table is verified by corroboration (our measurements + paper + Wikipedia), not by direct re-fetch; A-series rows and co-processor rows stay user-tagged

claim: Paper 2606.22283 and ane-guide map Pro/Max parts to the G tier letter (M3 Pro/Max->h15g, M4 Pro/Max->h16g, M5 Pro/Max->h17s) and use a bare 'h16' for M4 base; under Apple platform naming G is the base tier and bare H16 is not a platform name — our four-surface measurements (M4 base resolves h16g; coreai-build rejects bare h16 as Unknown architecture) side with Apple's naming, making the paper/guide map a tier-letter inversion, not our measurement error.
caveat: we measured two parts (M4 base, M5 Max) on 26A434; the paper may apply 'h1Ng' as its own runtime-identifier convention consistently — the dispute is specifically about mapping product rows to tier letters

claim: Apple M6 (announced 2026-08-25, released 2026-09-22, Mac mini only; 12-core CPU 2S+4P+6E, 12-core GPU with per-core Neural Accelerators, dual 16-core Neural Engine, 153.6/170 GB/s, TSMC 2nm) is the first base-only M generation - M6 Pro/Max are skipped with the high end continuing at M7 - and the h18g name was already accepted in the 26A434 AOT compile-surface we tested before the chip shipped.
source: https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/08/apple-introduces-m6-and-m5-ultra-for-a-big-leap-in-performance-and-ai-compute/ ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apple_M6 (fetched 2026-10-11); ours: h18g in e6 R4 menu (results/EXP-028-apple-tracer/results/e6_arch_surface_reconcile.txt)
caveat: platform name H18G, SoC ID T8152, codename Komodo and board ids are user-tagged (Apple Wiki / Bloomberg leak lineage) - the web-confirmed facts are the chip, date, product, and dual-16 ANE; h18g acceptance was in our menu, not a load test on H18 silicon

claim: The per-tier core ladder base=4 g=8 s=16 c=32 d=64 assigns NE counts to tier LETTERS, which under platform naming identify products not core counts; the paper itself separates marketing cores from physical compute sets (M1: marketing 16 vs 4 measured compute sets) and Apple now sells a dual-16-core ANE (M6), so num_nes and marketing counts measure different quantities and no division of one by the other is valid without first naming the quantity.
source: results/EXP-024-engine-attribution/raw/research-2026-10-06/ane_paper_sec20_sec33_extracts.md (28-target HAL table by byte offset; ~L21215 marketing-vs-compute-sets) + NAME-001/003 + CORE-003
caveat: this sharpens CORE-003, it does not close it: the exact quantity HAL counts remains open until the on-die probe runs

claim: The 5-target acceptance reported for the M4 mini versus 22 targets fed on the M5 Max is an artifact of the menus we chose to feed (mini: h15g/h16c/h16s/h17c + accepted h16g; Max: 22 named), not a machine-side difference: both boxes accepted exactly their own platform name and rejected everything else; ~6 further target names from the paper's 28-target table were never fed on either box.
caveat: equal-menu rerun on both boxes is registered (EXP-028 Next); until it runs, cite the e6 menus, not a 5-vs-21 machine contrast

claim: M-series has no dedicated ANE RAM chip - the Neural Engine shares the unified LPDDR pool; the real per-generation changes are (a) a higher-bandwidth ANE memory connection on M5 Pro/Max and (b) base-M5 pool bandwidth 153.6 GB/s versus M4's 120, while the ANE on-chip working set max_operand_bytes @0x1b8 (compiler name MemCacheSize) is 2 MB constant across the H13-H17 line; measured ANE-side DRAM throughput runs ~85-90 GB/s on M1-class versus ~145 GB/s weight-stream on M5/H17s.
caveat: user's 'dedicated RAM chip is bigger on M5' matches the connection-bandwidth change, not a discrete chip; per-machine ANE-reserve values on our two boxes are unread unprivileged (GAP, folded into the EXP-028 probe)
